title: Print-Ready Files for T-Shirts and Merch: What to Ask For
h1: Print-ready files for t-shirts and merch: what to ask your designer for
description: How to get merch designs that print well: print methods, vector vs high-resolution files, colors, sizes, mockups and a checklist before printing.
intro: A design that looks great on screen can print badly on a shirt, mug or tote bag. Colors shift, thin lines disappear and low-resolution images turn blurry. Most of these problems come from files that were not prepared for the way the product will actually be printed. This article explains what print-ready means for merchandise, what to tell your designer before they start, and what to check before you send files to a printer or print-on-demand service.

faq.q: What file format do printers want?
faq.a: Usually a vector file such as AI, EPS, SVG or PDF, or a high-resolution PNG with a transparent background.
Around 300 pixels per inch at the actual printed size is a common standard for raster files.

faq.q: Why do printed colors look different?
faq.a: Screens show light, while ink is absorbed by fabric. Fabric color and print method also change the result.

faq.q: Can I use any image I find online?
faq.a: No. You need the rights to every image, font and character in the design.
Yes. A single sample is the best way to check colors, size and placement before ordering in bulk.
